Method

Every question runs the same cycle: an observation from the record, a mechanism that would explain it, a falsification criterion frozen before the measurement, the run, the ruling quoted against that criterion, and an explicit statement of what the result does not close. A criterion chosen after the numbers are in is chosen to fit them, so the tooling refuses a verdict on a hypothesis that has no frozen criterion and refuses a criterion that cannot fail.

Refutation is the useful outcome. Inconclusive is reserved for a run that did not discriminate — never for one whose answer was unwelcome. A refuted thread is not a dead end: each refutation carries the variants it does not speak to, so a later reader can tell what was actually closed.

Verdicts across the whole record: INCONCLUSIVE 50, REFUTED 201, SUPPORTED 228, open 58.

Result in full
The frozen criterion reads: p10 below 25,400 applied positions/s REFUTES. The owned governor stopped the run at 104 accepted prefix rows (103 measured updates after the warm row) with a durable receipt whose order-statistic upper bound on the FINAL nearest-rank p10 over all 1,024 updates is 3,952.81 applied positions/s. That is a mathematical bound, not a projection: no completion of the remaining 921 updates could lift the p10 to 25,400. So the criterion is met by a factor of 6.4, and the campaign terminal of 80,000 by a factor of 20.2. K1-CAPTURED as implemented runs about 7x SLOWER than the standing governed 24,190.653, not 1.67x faster. There is NO governed 1,024-update number here: full_1024_rate is null and incomplete_1024 is true, so this arm does not join the count of the fifteen that carry one, and gate A does not move.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and the defect is MINE. The census priced what K1 REMOVES and never priced what it ADDS. treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling's 2026-09-12 amendment says in as many words that a replacement's own cost is an unknown the selection owes as a MEASUREMENT, never inferred from the incumbent and NEVER ASSUMED TO BE ZERO -- and my 1.670x assumed exactly zero. The SRL controller's own runtime is absent from every line of that arithmetic: 16 decisions per update, a policy and value forward per 256-position segment, the H=8 rollout bookkeeping, and the per-site branching the captured-regions caller must perform before each Q/O or FFN product. Measured 3,952.81 upper bound against a 24,190.653 incumbent is a 7x REGRESSION, so the unpriced additions dominate the priced removals by roughly an order of magnitude. NOT CLOSED: (a) the 70.75 percent FLOP reduction itself, which is arithmetic from frozen dimensions and stands unrefuted -- what is refuted is that it reaches the timeline through THIS caller; (b) the K1 MECHANISM, since a caller whose branching cost is proportional to site count is not the only possible one and this measures one implementation; (c) K2, K3', J1 and J3, which the order file prices off this census -- their rows inherit the same unpriced-addition defect and must not quote 1.670x; (d) whether the controller cost is fixed per update or scales with sites, which decides whether any caller can recover the reduction and is one no-card measurement away.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY TRACE IS READ FOR THIS CYCLE. UNIT is a GROUP keyed by (trace, kernel symbol, grid dimensions, block dimensions), so a symbol launched at two geometries is never compared against itself across them -- shape is excluded by the key rather than by hope. PREDICTOR is the DEVICE BUSY FRACTION over the 5,000 us immediately preceding each invocation's start, as a union of device intervals (kernel, gpu_memcpy, gpu_memset) clipped to that window divided by 5,000; the immediately preceding gap is NOT used, because clock and thermal state have a millisecond time constant and a microsecond gap cannot move it. SCORE per group is ordinary least squares of duration on busy fraction, read as the predicted duration at that group's OWN p90 busy over its predicted duration at its OWN p10 busy -- its observed span, never a fixed pair of thresholds. SCOREABILITY FLOOR, frozen: at least 200 invocations AND an interquartile range of at least 0.10 in busy fraction; a group whose predictor barely varies cannot score a slope in either direction and says so rather than passing vacuously. POOLED SCORE is the group scores weighted by group device time. VERDICT per arm: REFUTED (no load effect) if the pooled score is below 1.05; SUPPORTED at or above 1.05. SIGN CLAUSE, independent: at least two thirds of scoreable groups must share the sign of the pooled result, or the arm is INCONCLUSIVE because a 50/50 sign split is noise wearing a mean. COVERAGE FLOOR, independent: the arm is INCONCLUSIVE if fewer than three groups are scoreable or the scoreable groups carry below 0.30 of that arm's pooled device time -- the same floor the 2026-09-16 predecessor refused on, kept identical so the two are comparable. RESIDUAL is reported as a first-class number: the share of device time in unscoreable groups, with the reason each is unscoreable. BOTH ARMS are scored separately. If both clear their floors they must AGREE IN SIGN; a disagreement is reported as INCONCLUSIVE and as an instrument finding, never resolved by preferring one arm.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY TRACE IS READ FOR THIS CYCLE. IDENTICAL TO THE PREDECESSOR IN EVERYTHING BUT THE SCOREABILITY FLOOR, so the two are directly comparable: same unit (group keyed by trace, symbol, grid, block), same predictor (device busy fraction over the 5,000 us immediately preceding each invocation's start, union of kernel/gpu_memcpy/gpu_memset clipped to that window over 5,000), same score (OLS of duration on busy fraction, read as predicted duration at the group's OWN p90 busy over predicted at its OWN p10), same pooling (group scores weighted by group device time), same effect line (REFUTED below 1.05, SUPPORTED at or above), same sign clause (at least two thirds of scoreable groups share the pooled sign, else INCONCLUSIVE), same coverage floor (fewer than 3 scoreable groups OR scoreable share below 0.30 of that arm's pooled device time -> INCONCLUSIVE), same per-arm scoring and the same agreement clause across arms. THE ONE CHANGE: the 200-invocation floor is REPLACED by a RESOLUTION floor. A group is scoreable if its busy-fraction IQR is at least 0.10 AND its design can resolve a 5 percent change in duration across its own observed predictor span -- formally, the standard error of the fitted slope multiplied by the group's p90-minus-p10 busy span, divided by the predicted duration at its p10, is at most 0.05. THE FLOOR DEPENDS ONLY ON PREDICTOR SPREAD AND RESIDUAL NOISE AND NEVER ON THE FITTED SLOPE'S VALUE: a group whose slope is exactly zero and one whose slope is large are scoreable or unscoreable on identical grounds, so the floor cannot select groups by the size of the effect it is measuring. No invocation count appears in any clause. Counts are still REPORTED per group so the change in the admitted population is readable. THE PREDECESSOR'S INCONCLUSIVE STANDS AS ISSUED; this is a named successor, not a repair applied in place, and if this design also fails its coverage floor that is an INCONCLUSIVE too and not a third attempt at the same answer.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY COMPILATION. Both kernels are compiled at the PRODUCTION call-site configuration read from src/ember/model/ember_v0_grouped_capture.py lines 91-118 -- BM=64, BN=128, BK=32, num_warps=4, and NC=0 for _weights -- not at the default constexpr values in their signatures. For each kernel the resident-block ceiling is computed for ALL FOUR limiters on compute capability 8.9: registers (65,536 32-bit registers per SM, allocated per warp in 256-register granules), static shared memory (102,400 bytes per SM), the resident-thread cap (1,536) and the resident-warp cap (48), plus the 24-block-per-SM cap. REFUTED if the REGISTER ceiling is not STRICTLY the smallest of those five for BOTH kernels -- that is, refuted if for either kernel some other limiter binds at or below the register ceiling, because then halving register pressure buys no occupancy and the lever's name describes a mechanism its kernels do not have. Also REFUTED if the report omits any of the five ceilings, since publishing only the register ceiling would make registers binding by construction. Also REFUTED if either kernel reports n_spills greater than zero, because a spilling kernel is bound by local-memory traffic rather than by occupancy and the lever's arithmetic would then be about a different quantity. Also REFUTED if the compiled configuration does not match the production call site exactly.

Result in full
The frozen criterion reads: 'REFUTED if the REGISTER ceiling is not STRICTLY the smallest of those five for BOTH kernels -- that is, refuted if for either kernel some other limiter binds at or below the register ceiling, because then halving register pressure buys no occupancy'. It does not bind strictly, for either kernel, and the reason is a TIE. Measured at the production configuration BM=64, BN=128, BK=32, num_warps=4: _rows uses 128 registers per thread and _weights 126, both with ZERO spilled bytes, and both use 24,576 bytes of static shared memory. On compute capability 8.9 that gives, per kernel, a register ceiling of 4 resident blocks per SM and a SHARED-MEMORY ceiling of exactly 4 as well, against 12 from the resident-thread cap, 12 from the resident-warp cap and 24 from the block cap. Registers and shared memory bind TOGETHER at 4 blocks per SM, which is 16 of 48 warps, an occupancy ceiling of 0.3333. So the lever two_register_limited_kernels_halved is INERT ON ITS OWN: halving register pressure on either kernel moves nothing, because shared memory holds occupancy at exactly the same 4 blocks. The premise is half true -- registers ARE a binding limiter -- and the lever as named is not, because relieving one of two tied limiters changes no ceiling. Every other clause holds: all five ceilings are reported rather than the register one alone; neither kernel spills; the compiled configuration is the call site's at ember_v0_grouped_capture.py lines 91 and 115, not the 32/64/32 defaults in the signatures; and an absent register count is refused as UNSUPPORTED rather than reported as a zero, which fired on the first run and was cured before this verdict. THE REFUTATION RUNS AGAINST MY OWN ARM: this is the third lever of the only above-bar combination on the board.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND THE SUCCESSOR IT NAMES. (a) THE NAMED SUCCESSOR IS A JOINT LEVER, not a register one: registers and shared memory tie at 4 blocks per SM, so the only treatment that can raise occupancy at all must relieve BOTH. num_stages=3 at a 24,576-byte shared footprint is the obvious handle and it is UNMEASURED -- fewer stages lowers shared memory and may raise or lower register pressure, and which way is a compilation question answerable by the same instrument at a different configuration. That successor is named and not run here. (b) OCCUPANCY IS NOT TIME. Even a treatment that doubles resident blocks does not halve either kernel's duration; occupancy and duration are different quantities and the lever's ceiling arithmetic is separately owed. Nothing here prices anything. (c) A COMPILED CEILING IS NOT AN ACHIEVED OCCUPANCY. These are hardware maxima; what the scheduler made resident during the governed step is unmeasured and no occupancy counter is read anywhere on this campaign. (d) IT DOES NOT REFUTE THE 1.6940x COMBINATION, it refutes the NAME and the assumed mechanism of one of its three levers. The combination's factor is inherited arithmetic about device time and stands as such; what falls is the claim that the third lever's gain comes from register relief, and with it the plausibility that the lever is implementable as described. Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY COMPILATION. The grid is the full cross product of num_stages in {1,2,3,4,5} and num_warps in {4,8} with BM=64, BN=128, BK=32 held at the production values, compiled for BOTH kernels (_weights at NC=0). The frozen metric is RESIDENT WARPS PER SM = (minimum resident blocks per SM over all five limiters) x num_warps, capped at 48, and every one of the five ceilings is reported for every configuration. A configuration is ADMISSIBLE only if BOTH kernels compile and BOTH report ZERO spilled bytes; an inadmissible configuration is reported with its reason and never silently dropped. REFUTED if no admissible configuration reaches resident warps STRICTLY GREATER THAN 16 for BOTH kernels, where 16 is the production configuration's measured ceiling. Also REFUTED if the report ranks configurations by resident BLOCKS rather than by resident WARPS, since that metric would score a warp-count change as an improvement or a regression when it is neither. Also REFUTED if any configuration's tile differs from 64x128x32, because that would be a different treatment and not this one. Also REFUTED if a register count or a spill count comes back UNSUPPORTED for any compiled configuration and is entered as a zero rather than excluding that configuration and saying so.

Result in full
The frozen criterion reads: 'REFUTED if no admissible configuration reaches resident warps STRICTLY GREATER THAN 16 for BOTH kernels'. One does. num_stages=2 with num_warps=8 at the frozen 64x128x32 tile reaches 24 resident warps per SM on both kernels -- occupancy ceiling 0.5000 against the production 0.3333, a 1.5x increase in the ceiling -- with ZERO spilled bytes on either kernel. It gets there by relieving both tied limiters at once, which is exactly what the predecessor's tie said was required: registers per thread fall from 128 to 78 on _rows and from 126 to 80 on _weights, and static shared memory falls from 24,576 to 16,384 bytes. Every other clause holds: all ten configurations are ranked by RESIDENT WARPS and not by resident blocks, which matters because three distinct configurations tie with production at 16 warps while differing in blocks; the tile is 64x128x32 in every row; all ten compiled with readable register and spill counts so none was excluded and none was entered as a zero. The run also shows the metric earning its keep -- num_stages=1 with num_warps=8 reports 16 warps, identical to production, where a block-ranked report would have called it a regression. Deliberate red: the bar raised to the hardware maximum of 48 resident warps refuses at exit 1, into a separate receipt path so it cannot clobber the green one.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND THE SUCCESSOR IT NAMES. (a) OCCUPANCY IS NOT TIME, and this is the whole gap between a candidate and a treatment. A 1.5x ceiling says more warps MAY be resident; it does not say either kernel runs faster, and num_stages=2 gives strictly less latency hiding per warp than 3, which can run slower at higher occupancy. The named successor is a measured DURATION for both kernels at stages=2/warps=8 against stages=3/warps=4 at the production shapes, and no ceiling arithmetic is stated until that exists -- an incumbent class's time bounds the SAVINGS available and bounds a replacement's own cost from neither direction. (b) IT IS A DECLARED NUMERICAL TREATMENT AND NEEDS THE LICENCE INSTRUMENT. Changing num_warps changes how the output tile is split across warps and changing num_stages changes accumulation order; _weights carries an explicit bf16 rounding boundary per chunk in its NC branch, written to match a reference. So this cannot be run as an arm on the strength of an occupancy number -- it is a candidate for the licence pair, not a shortcut past it. (c) THE SHAPES USED TO COMPILE ARE NOT THE PRODUCTION SHAPES. Register allocation does not depend on them, which is why the sweep is valid for ceilings; a DURATION measurement is meaningless at 256x256x256 and must use the governed geometry. (d) THE TILE STAYS FROZEN. The campaign's registered 64x128 grouped-tile candidate is a different treatment and is not this one; combining them is a third thing and is unmeasured. (e) ONE TOOLCHAIN, ONE ARCHITECTURE, no matched-run variation, so nothing here is a licensed ceiling under the governed-run evidence contract. (f) IT DOES NOT REVIVE THE LEVER two_register_limited_kernels_halved, whose premise stays refuted; it names a DIFFERENT lever -- a joint pipeline-and-warp change -- that the refutation pointed at. Limitations, and what this does not close
THE SUCCESSOR THIS NAMES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE. The arithmetic here is not specific to the grouped class: for ANY class, elimination clears a bar B only if the class's share of device time is at least 1 - 1/B, which at B=1.50 is 0.3333. That threshold is computable for every class in the same table in one pass, and it decides -- before any treatment is named -- which single-class confinements are refused by arithmetic and which are not. THE NAMED SUCCESSOR IS THAT WHOLE-TABLE BOUND: every class, its share, its total-elimination ceiling, and a binary of whether any confinement to it could ever clear the bar. Widen before narrowing; running it on one class and stopping is how a vocabulary misses the answer. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. (a) IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT A STACK. The 1.5x bar governs a STANDALONE arm. stages=2/warps=8 stays lawful and worth pricing AS A STACK MEMBER, and its duration successor is still worth running for that purpose -- what is now refused is dispatching it as a lone arm, which the operator's clause already forbids for any pre-stated ceiling below 1.5x. (b) IT IS A DEVICE-TIME BOUND. The governed step is larger than the device union, so the step-level ratio is SMALLER -- the direction that strengthens the refusal -- but no profiled/governed composition is made and no step figure is quoted. (c) ONE TRACE, ONE GEOMETRY, ONE HEAD (20338ddc). A different geometry or head can carry a different share and the bound is recomputed there, never carried across. (d) IT DOES NOT SAY THE CLASS CAN BE ELIMINATED. Elimination is the arithmetic ceiling, not a proposal, and no kernel replacement is named. (e) IT DOES NOT PRICE THE OCCUPANCY CANDIDATE. Occupancy is not time; the duration measurement is what prices it, and this only says what that price can at most be worth. (f) Gate A is unmoved and remains UNMET at p10 24,190.653 positions/s; composite 10 percent.

Limitations, and what this does not close
THE DEFECT MY OWN CRITERION CARRIED, NAMED FIRST BECAUSE IT IS MINE. The supported-if clause read strictly positive for the population overlap, and 26.3 us on a smaller union of 66,146.1 is 0.0004 -- functionally zero. A clause that fires on any value above zero cannot discriminate a real overlap from measurement dust, and it is the same shape as a strict-order clause that counts ties as inversions: it produces a verdict without carrying information. That is not a small number, it is an ARITHMETIC IDENTITY I had not seen: two intervals that cross are merged into one interval by a union, and clipping the later one's start to the earlier one's end leaves the merged interval identical. A same-stream crossing CANNOT understate a union. So the campaign-wide flattery worry is retired at its source, whatever the crossings turn out to be, and it was retired by an instrument built to answer a different question. WHAT THE DISTRIBUTION ACTUALLY SAYS, INCLUDING THE PART THAT REFUSES THE ROUNDING STORY AS STATED. The POSITIVE-gap control is the discriminator I froze for this, and it is decisive about the real clock: positive gaps have p01 and p10 both at 0.0312 us, which is 1/32 us, so the device timestamps tick at about 31.25 ns and NOT at the 0.001 us the trace's decimal places advertise. A third account fits both halves better and neither of my two did: CUPTI's begin and end timestamps for adjacent kernels on one queue can be recorded with small independent errors, mostly a few ticks and occasionally much larger when a sample is delayed. WHAT THE REFUTATION LEAVES STANDING, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING MEASURED TODAY. The question this run cannot answer and the next one can: are the slow updates PERIODIC, and if so at what interval. Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
The criterion is frozen on a join between the slowest decile of the launch-configuration-plus-reshape run and every numeric per-update counter its own rows carry, analysis-only, no card and no lease. Counters are taken as they appear in the rows rather than chosen after inspection, and the phase-seconds fields are EXCLUDED from the SUPPORTED decision because forward, backward and optimizer seconds are constitutive of a slow update rather than explanatory of it -- a slow update is slow in some phase by definition, and crediting that as a finding would be a gate comparing a value to its own source. SUPPORTED if at least one NON-PHASE counter has a slow-decile mean differing from the fast-nine-decile mean by a factor of at least 2.0 in either direction, or, for a counter whose fast-decile mean is zero, has a strictly positive slow-decile mean. A factor that large on a named counter identifies a mechanism. REFUTED if NO non-phase counter reaches that factor, which says the extra time is not accompanied by any recorded activity and the dispersion is inside the kernels. INCONCLUSIVE, explicitly and in advance, if a counter reaches the factor but is constant across the whole run, or varies but is identical in distribution between the two groups under inspection of its own values -- a factor computed on a near-zero denominator is arithmetic rather than evidence, and I would rather say so than report it. REFUTED, separately and on instrument grounds rather than on the hypothesis, if the slow set is not exactly 102 updates, or if the counters cannot be read for all 1,024 updates, or if the union of the slow set and the fast set is not the full 1,024 with no overlap. The residual clause: every key present in the rows must be classified as phase, non-phase numeric, or non-numeric, and the count of each is REPORTED, so a counter the join silently could not read shows up as a number rather than as a silence.

On slow updates the host forward time (0.1226) EXCEEDS the CUDA forward time (0.1086), meaning the host has stopped running ahead and is blocking inside the forward path. The dispersion that costs this run its p10 is a forward-path host stall, not a device-side cost, and backward and optimizer are untouched by it. Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
The criterion is frozen on the per-update token delta, defined as cursor_after.token_offset minus cursor_before.token_offset, computed for all 1,024 captured updates of the launch-configuration-plus-reshape run, analysis-only, no card and no lease. SUPPORTED if the slow decile's mean token delta differs from the fast nine deciles' mean token delta by at least 20 percent in either direction. That is the threshold at which packing plausibly accounts for a 2.04x CUDA forward difference, and it is stated before the numbers are read. REFUTED if the two means differ by less than 5 percent, which says the slow updates consume essentially the same data as the fast ones and the extra forward time has no data-volume behind it -- making it a true stall. INCONCLUSIVE, explicitly and in advance, for the band between 5 and 20 percent, because a modest packing difference neither accounts for a 2.04x factor nor rules out a contribution, and choosing either reading on that evidence would be choosing the answer. REFUTED, separately and on instrument grounds rather than on the hypothesis, if either cursor field is missing or non-numeric on any update, if the deltas are not all non-negative, if the slow set is not exactly 102 updates, or if the recomputed p10, p50 and p90 of the run do not reproduce its own summary to within one part in ten thousand. The last clause is the identity check that the series read is the series the summary was computed from.

One update carries a delta of -4,190,208, the data cursor wrapping its shard, and the criterion refuses rather than letting me decide after the fact whether one row is discountable. The identity clause passed at 0.00e+00, the slow set is exactly 102, and no cursor field is missing, so the instrument is otherwise sound and only this clause fired.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and it is the answer arriving through the side door. The join reports exactly TWO distinct token deltas across all 1,024 updates: 4,096 and the single wrap. So document packing is CONSTANT, every update consumes identical data, and the slow decile is not doing more work because it was handed more data. The substantive hypothesis is therefore dead on this run's own numbers even though the criterion refuted on the wrap row, and a successor excluding that one row would rule REFUTED substantively rather than on instrument grounds -- worth stating so nobody re-runs it expecting a different answer. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE STALL. CUDA forward rises 2.0428x on the slow decile while the data is byte-for-byte the same volume, so the device genuinely executes more or slower work on identical input. That excludes a data explanation and leaves capture re-entry or a conditional fallback path as the live candidates, neither of which any recorded per-update counter would show. WHY THIS CYCLE IS NOT THE NEXT ONE. The operator's direction at 02:12 PM and again at 02:16 PM LA is the 80,000 terminal, and this stall is worth about five percent. The successor that matters is not this one: my own route arithmetic capped at 55,783 positions per second, and it held POSITIONS PER OPTIMIZER STEP fixed at 4,096 throughout while pricing only precision. That premise has never been measured. If device milliseconds per position fall as positions per step rise, the batch term and the precision term MULTIPLY, and the cap I published is an artifact of an unexamined constant rather than a property of the card.

SUPPORTED against the frozen criterion, both clauses, quoted. Clause one read: SUPPORTED if the summed fp16-with-fp16-accumulate time is at most 0.75x the summed bf16 time. Measured 1,488.17 us against 2,334.16 us over the model own seven dense site shapes, which is 0.6376x -- inside the line. So switching operands to fp16 buys 4.6 percent and switching the ACCUMULATOR buys the rest, which is the mechanism this cycle named and is the one that matters, because it means the lever is a compute-type flag over an fp16 operand pair and not a quantization scheme. THE COMPARISON AGAINST FP8 IS THE POINT AND IT IS DIRECT. FP8 measured 1.0134x under capture earlier today because its compiled quantize cost 149.06 us against a 41.76 us scaled GEMM -- a per-activation-byte tax against a per-FLOP saving. This arm pays no such tax: there is no amax, no scale and no cast kernel, and the 1.5685x is what the same card returns at the same shapes when the rate is reached without one. ONE SHAPE REGRESSES AND IT IS NAMED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY. kv_proj, the narrow n=256 projection, is 0.739x -- SLOWER under fp16 accumulation, 24.8 us against 18.3. It is 18 us of a 2,334 us total so it does not move the sum, but a per-site dtype selection must exclude it rather than apply the flag globally, and a global flag would take that site backwards. THIS MEASURES DURATION ONLY AND LICENSES NOTHING. fp16 operands are a declared numerical treatment with a narrower dynamic range than bf16, which is a training-stability question this cycle does not touch; the no-worse-learning licence would need its own 64-update pair against the bf16 parent.
Limitations, and what this does not close
SUCCESSOR, and it is a governed arm rather than another probe: apply fp16 operands with fp16 accumulation at the CIADecoder dense projection funnel and measure 1,024 governed updates. The funnel already exists -- CIADecoder has zero nn.Linear and every dense projection goes through one _linear function, which was wired this afternoon for the FP8 arm behind an env flag and falls back to exactly F.linear when unselected. An fp16-accumulate arm is a strictly smaller change than the FP8 one that funnel was built for: cast the operand pair at the funnel and set the compute-type flag, with no quantize path, no scale, no weight cache and no autograd Function. The kv_proj exclusion is part of the arm, not a caveat: that site measured 0.739x and a global application would take it backwards, so the funnel selects per site by output width. THE STEP-LEVEL CEILING, with its premise stated separately from its arithmetic as a ceiling must be. PREMISE: the flag binds cuBLAS dense mm with fp16 operands and does not reach the Triton grouped-expert kernels, the flash attention backward, or any non-arithmetic kernel. Under that premise the affected population is the dense aten::mm class, 50.92 ms of the 154.83 ms governed device time, which at the measured 1.5685x becomes 32.46 ms for a step of 150.86 ms and 27,150 applied positions per second, 1.122x. Extending it to the grouped expert kernels, which are Triton and would need their accumulator changed in source rather than by a flag, reaches 1.183x; including the attention backward reaches 1.218x. Those are ceilings assuming perfect application and they are bounded below by nothing. WHAT THE FLOOR CHECK SAYS ABOUT 80,000, recorded here because it is the most useful thing this cycle produced and it is not a refutation. At the 240 TF/s these arms actually achieved, the unchanged 10.197 TF/step of arithmetic takes 42.5 ms. Add the measured 14.49 ms of non-device time and the step is 56.98 ms, which is 71,888 positions per second -- with EVERY non-arithmetic device kernel assumed removed or perfectly hidden. So the terminal sits just outside a perfect-everything floor at today achieved efficiency, and inside it if non-device time also falls: at 9.2 ms it is 79,245. The three conditions are therefore all live and all binding together, and the one this cycle did not move is condition B, efficiency against the rate, which stayed at 0.73 where 0.841 is needed.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING, AT ITS SOURCE. The verdict stands REFUTED on the frozen clause and does not move. The measured fixed share today is 0.1669 and the step is 164.33 ms. The campaign's own progress shrank both the step and the fixed fraction inside it, so the lever that amortises fixed cost got smaller as the step got faster. This is the standing law that an inherited factor must be repriced against the current measurement rather than carried, and it is the second lever in two days whose inherited price was wrong by more than a factor of two in the direction that made it attractive. WHAT THIS DECIDES FOR THE 80,000 TERMINAL, stated as arithmetic over the split above with its premise separate. 80,000 positions per second at 4,096 positions is a 51.2 ms step; the fixed terms alone are 27.42 ms, which is 53.6 percent of that entire budget. So at today's geometry forward and backward would have to fall from 136.91 ms to 23.78 ms, a factor of 5.76. Raising documents per step dilutes the fixed terms and lowers that requirement: at eight documents the required factor on forward and backward is 3.65, at sixteen it is 3.09, and in the limit it is 2.674. THE PREMISE, kept separate from the arithmetic: that forward and backward scale linearly with documents at a held sequence length of 1,024, and that the optimizer and host terms do not scale at all. The optimizer half is structural. The linearity half is an assumption that holds for adding documents and would NOT hold for lengthening them, since attention is quadratic in sequence length. SO THE TERMINAL'S REQUIREMENT IS NOW ONE NUMBER RATHER THAN THREE CONDITIONS: forward and backward device time must fall by a factor between 2.674 and 5.76 depending on documents per step, and every remaining route must act on that 136.91 ms. The contract lever is not a route to the terminal, but it is not worthless either -- it lowers the factor the real routes must deliver from 5.76 to 3.65 at eight documents, which is the difference between two levers stacking to enough and not. It remains a learning-contract change and therefore the operator's to rule; what has changed is that it is now correctly priced as an ENABLER of the arithmetic rather than as a route to the terminal, and it is not worth his attention on its own.
Limitations, and what this does not close
Ruled. The asymptote of positions per optimizer step is the variable-rate term, so geometry alone cannot reach the terminal. Not closed: positions per step is a LEARNING-CONTRACT change and remains the operator to rule, with its projected gain stated and never taken silently.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY RUN. The experiment is a LADDER of governed measurements at ONE head and one data plan, differing in exactly one field of geometry.json: documents_per_step in 4, 8, 16, 32, each at sequence_length 1024, warm_steps 1 and measured_steps 256. The 4-document rung is the MATCHED CONTROL and it runs in the same job, at the same head, on the same data, with the same statistic, because the single most expensive error on this campaign tonight was scoring arms against a comparator from a different head. Update COUNT is matched at 256 across rungs so the nearest-rank p10 is taken over populations of equal size; 256 is below gate A's 1,024, so NO number from this cycle is a gate A number and none is reported as one. CLAUSE 1, EXECUTION, decided first and from each rung's own receipt rather than from the geometry file it was handed. For every rung, applied_positions divided by measured_updates must equal documents_per_step times 1024 exactly. A geometry field is a REQUEST; the quotient is the EVENT. Any rung whose quotient does not match its request is INCONCLUSIVE for that rung and is never read as a result, because a rung that silently ran a different geometry has measured something else under this rung's name. CLAUSE 2, THE CONTROL IS LOAD-BEARING. If the 4-document rung does not execute and satisfy clause 1, the WHOLE cycle is INCONCLUSIVE regardless of what the other rungs return. A ratio against a comparator from another head or another job is exactly the defect being repaired. CLAUSE 3, REFUTED: clause 1 and clause 2 hold, and the highest executing rung's p10 is BELOW 1.15x the 4-document rung's p10. Below 1.15x the fixed per-invocation term is too small a share for geometry to act on the kernel-count row at all, and the lever is refuted as a way of reaching row 1 without authoring a fusion. CLAUSE 4, SUPPORTED: clause 1 and clause 2 hold, and the highest executing rung's p10 is AT OR ABOVE 1.24x the 4-document rung's p10 -- the low end of the asymptote range the mechanism predicts from the class table, taking the elementwise class as wholly scaling. CLAUSE 5, THE DISCRIMINATION FLOOR, frozen here so it cannot be chosen after the numbers are in: a ratio strictly between 1.15x and 1.24x is INCONCLUSIVE. No matched-run variation exists on any governed number in this campaign and every head's within-run p50-to-p10 gap is about 6 percent, so a ratio inside that band is not resolvable by one run per rung. That is a statement about this instrument, not a hedge against an unwelcome number. CLAUSE 6, RESOURCE REFUSAL IS A RESULT AND NOT AN INCONCLUSIVE. What the instrument own per-row output shows, and what the aggregate hid. That is 9314 us per step at 152 to 260 GB/s on a card whose DRAM rate is about 1008, with 864 of the launches carrying a non-contiguous operand. The launch counts match one launch per resident expert per weight matrix, so this is the expert weight-gradient accumulation path reading a transposed buffer. An elementwise add of the same elements is bit-identical whichever order memory is walked in, so a layout repair here is bit-exact and needs no licence pair. The successor is registered as a per-row cycle over exactly those four rows with a population that excludes graph-annotation joins by construction, and it is NOT this cycle re-run with a wider bound.

Limitations, and what this does not close
The successor is an INSTRUMENT REPAIR, not a treatment. The interval union is sensitive to where the profiler window lands and to every scheduling gap inside the step; per-window coverage in one reference arm ranged 0.8019 to 0.8986, which is a 10 point swing in what fraction of the window the union even covers. The successor hypothesis is therefore an ATTRIBUTION of the largest unexamined non-GEMM class, elementwise at 32,582.4 us/step, because it has no measured ceiling and nothing on the books has ever instrumented it. Criterion, frozen before the run

All three frozen clauses PASS. Null-pair spread 1.55 percent against a 15 percent ceiling. Rise 17.660 us per position against max(F=0.647, 1.80) = 1.800. Rise 17.660 against the half-predicted 2.650. The two-point fit puts the non-scaling population at 72333.4 us per optimizer step, 42 percent of the 170839.0 us step, against my predicted 21667. I under-predicted by 3.3x and the criterion cleared by 6.7x, so the verdict is not marginal -- and I record the OVERSHOOT as part of it, because a prediction wrong by 3.3x in the favourable direction is exactly the shape that deserves distrust rather than celebration.
Limitations, and what this does not close
THE CONFOUND, which the totals cannot resolve and which bounds every use of this result. Two different things produce a cost that fails to halve when positions halve. FIXED work is set by the parameter count or by the step itself and is collected by paying it less often. SUBLINEAR work is proportional in principle but runs inefficiently at the smaller size, and amortization collects NONE of it, because at depth N you run N full-size passes and pay the full-size cost each time. A two-point comparison of TOTALS cannot tell them apart, so 72333.4 us is an UPPER BOUND on the collectible population and must never be quoted as the lever size. Per class they do separate, and the class table is the real finding. Ratios of docs2 to docs4 cost: optimizer 1.078 and grouped_rows 0.919 are FIXED-like; gemm_dense 0.617, elementwise 0.667, grouped_weights 0.611, triton 0.675, other 0.606, gather 0.557 are scaling, though none reaches the ideal 0.5, so sublinearity is present everywhere. The optimizer at 1.078 is genuinely fixed and its 20964 us is collectible. The finding I did not expect is grouped_rows at 0.919: the grouped expert kernel costs almost the same for half the tokens, which is the signature of per-step EXPERT WEIGHT STREAMING whose bytes are set by the expert population rather than by token count. NOT CLOSED: whether grouped_rows is fixed or merely badly underutilised, which decides whether it is collectible at all and which needs a third point at docs=1 or 3 rather than another two-point fit. NOT CLOSED: the amortization ceiling itself. The proportional floor is 24.05 us per position, so perfect amortization of everything reaches 41580 positions per second and NO FURTHER -- 1.64x of today, the largest single lever measured on this campaign, and still not the terminal on its own. ALSO NOT CLOSED, and it changes which mechanism is right: gradient accumulation does not collect weight streaming, because each pass re-reads the weights. What collects it is more tokens sharing ONE weight read, and tokens per forward are capped at 4096 by a declared guard at ember_v0_residency.py line 713 and three sibling guards in ember_v0_decoder.py. Raising that constant is a context-length change to a canonical architecture and is not a throughput trick. The lawful shape is a BATCH dimension of independent 4096-position contexts, which multiplies tokens per weight read while changing no per-sequence semantics. That is the successor worth authoring, and it is large.

Measured p10 61,749.0 (p50 69,480, p90 72,782) with prefetch, against 70,009 p10 for threaded decode without it. Prefetch made it WORSE: cuda forward 11.2 -> 12.2 ms and backward 21.5 -> 24.8 ms median, consistent with 8 decode pool threads x 16 intra-op threads oversubscribing the 32 cores while the host issues eager work. Limitations, and what this does not close

Successor: trace the A1 step and attribute that idle to step start, eager segments, and context exit. Prefetch wiring is to be reverted; threaded decode kept.

AMENDED per this seat mail 38464 (methodological correction, arrived after mail 38465's report but before this update): the original stem_survives/options_only classification was a binary substring-match heuristic that presupposed a conclusion. Corrected measurement uses exact tokenizer per-token character offsets (Tokenizer.encode(...).offsets) to classify each over-cap row's question-stem retention as complete/partial/none, counts options fully retained, and checks whether the answer-letter's own option text survives -- broken down per dataset_id. Receipt: seat record: caption-truncation-census-20260928.json (schema v2). Frozen claim, reworded per this seat's instruction: truncation occurs at rate 68.97% (121736/176518 answer-scoped rows), with retention distribution: 0% of over-cap rows retain the COMPLETE question stem in any dataset; the majority retain it PARTIALLY (arxivqa 41.7% partial/58.3% none -- arxivqa is 77% of all rows and 97% of all over-cap rows; ai2d 77.5%/22.5%; scienceqa 75%/25%; m3exam-english 63.4%/36.6%; mmbench-dev-scienceqa 70.9%/29.1%). Options are mostly fully retained (82.6%-93.0% across datasets) and the answer-letter's own option text stays intact 82.6%-96.5% of the time. This is NOT "options-only" (the prior wording) and this census does not itself establish D-cause -- it establishes the truncation rate and retention shape only.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
answer rows exceed 58 tokens (contrast real). Stop and re-rule if the first arm runs above 0.25 s per update. ## Frozen criterion (unchanged from 41515; pasted verbatim into loop predict before claim) - caption wrong-real (NLL wrong-image minus NLL real-image): REFUTED if the treatment does not exceed the control by 0.05 nats. - MMMU real-missing and real-wrong, n=847, no score bar. The statistic is the difference-in-differences: (treatment real-minus-contrast) minus (control real-minus-contrast). - Its interval is computed from PAIRED per-question outcomes, matched across every condition and both arms. It comes from a paired item bootstrap, resampling questions and never conditions independently. All per-question correctness vectors are saved in the receipt. - Exact method (the counterpart seat 42180): the interval is a 95% percentile interval over 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples of the 847 questions, seed 0. It is applied to control/treatment, and separately to the control/control null pair. The null pair is the INSTRUMENT CHECK, not an additive term. If its interval excludes 0, the run is REFUSED as non-discriminating before any verdict, and that check is applied before the treatment pair is read. - 0.0154, the one-score standard error, is NOT that interval. It is kept only as a preset OPERATING THRESHOLD: the treatment's statistic must exceed +0.0154 to count as a rise. (the counterpart seat 42166 correction, adopted before any predict.) - DECISION ORDER (amended 2026-10-01 02:06 AM LA on the counterpart seat 42760; mutually exclusive, first match wins; s = the statistic, [L,U] = its 95% interval): 1. Null-pair interval excludes 0 -> REFUSED (instrument does not discriminate; no verdict read). 2. U < 0 -> REFUTED-HARM (treatment worse than control). 3. s > +0.0154 and L > 0 -> SUPPORTED (a rise past the operating threshold). 4. s > +0.0154 and L <= 0 -> INCONCLUSIVE (point past the threshold, interval includes 0). 5. U < +0.0154 -> REFUTED (failed the preset bar; NOT evidence of harm). 6. Otherwise -> INCONCLUSIVE. Counterexamples: s=-0.002, [-0.010,0.005] -> rule 5 REFUTED. s=0.020, [-0.004,0.044] -> rule 4 INCONCLUSIVE. s=0.010, [-0.010,0.030] -> rule 6 INCONCLUSIVE. s=0.030, [0.006,0.054] -> rule 3 SUPPORTED. - Arm values (02:20 AM LA ruling WITHDRAWN 02:28 AM LA on the counterpart seat 42781: the carrier has no separate stem switch; the answer cap IS the treatment, so equal caps made the arms identical). Corrected, at carrier da91b549 (the counterpart seat source PASS 42781): CONTROL cap 58 (EMBER_ANSWER_CAPTION_TOKENS=58 set explicitly), TREATMENT cap 79 (the largest cap that fits 7 pairs: 7*(1+64+1+79+1)=1022 <= 1024); both arms 7 pairs per document (EMBER_PAIRS_PER_DOCUMENT=7; production is 8, so this is NOT production geometry) and image row start 149,664 in the seed-2163 order of manifest de32a445 (592,640 rows). 149,664 is the row OFFSET R: the first consumed row is (149,664 + 7*S) mod 592,640 with S the parent step, and the prep receipt binds S and that first row (the counterpart seat 42785). The null pair is control/control at cap 58. This is a CONTEXT-LENGTH observation: it does not prove the whole question survives. Loss-bearing targets per answer-scoped pair stay two (answer letter + end token) in both arms; the treatment adds conditioning tokens only (the counterpart seat 42785, image_text_stream.py 193-201). Before the card, the prep-only proof reports, for the actually selected answer rows, the count and fraction whose encoded length exceeds 58 (retained tokens differ between arms), and separately the full-fit fractions at 58 and 79. The dispatch receipt's emitted geometry must equal these values per arm or the run is REFUSED. The probe rows are NOT unseen: the lineage has consumed the manifest about 8.25 times. The

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
the gate D binding env is absent or unsourced, the evaluator does not record the executed image condition, fewer than the full 847-item set is scored in any condition, the pointer changes during the run, or the real-image accuracy lies outside [0.22, 0.31]. seat record: verdict.json

Prediction calibrated: binding sourced, condition recorded per run, 847 items in each of real/missing/wrong, pointer byte-equal, real-image accuracy 0.292 inside [0.22, 0.31]. Capability criterion ember-3b-image-capability-v1 result: FAILED (mmmu-score.json), claim_status NON_ADMISSIBLE_RAW_PREDICTIONS; real 0.292 is above 0.2857 by less than one SE (0.0156) so not gate D met. Real minus missing +0.010 and real minus wrong +0.012, both under one SE: image dependence NOT established. Instrument defect: the wrong-image shift 423 leaves 80 of 847 documents identical to real (wrong control 767-effective); numerators 247/239/237 are implied by rounded scores, the receipts hold no correct flag. Next image run: a derangement with zero fixed points, correct flags and paired discordant counts. Receipt seat record: verdict.json.
Limitations, and what this does not close
Plain reading: the seventeenth child scored 0.292 with the real image, 0.282 with no image and 0.28 with a swapped image on 847 items. The gaps are under one standard error, so the test does not show the model uses the image. The swapped-image control left 80 of 847 items unchanged, so it was a weaker control than intended; the next run fixes that.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
REFUTED IF the DURATION-WEIGHTED contested figure under the RETIRES-EVERYTHING scenario EXCEEDS 7,452.9 us per step -- the composition fails under the reading most hostile to it once the count-share assumption is corrected. Given the cycle-40 inputs (1,172.3 elementwise gaps retired, 46.7 optimizer gaps, 7,437.7 gaps per step, 32,700.0 us idle lever) that threshold is crossed at a measured ratio of about 1.406, so a ratio above ~1.406 refutes and a ratio at or below it supports. ALSO REFUTED, independently of any ratio, IF THE ELEMENTWISE-FOLLOWED GAP SET IS EMPTY: the instrument exits non-zero rather than publishing a zero or undefined ratio, because a selector that matched nothing and a genuine zero are opposite in meaning and identical in arithmetic. The 7,452.9 threshold is unchanged from cycles 38, 39 and 40 and derives from the bar, not from anything read here: 1.5x on the 0.16376 s governed step needs 54,586.7 us removed, the naive three-lever stack is 62,039.6 us, margin exactly 7,452.9 us.
Instrument

Same window scoping, same kernel filter and the same FOLLOWED-BY retirement rule cycles 38-40 used, because a ratio computed over a different population would not correct the number it is meant to correct. Evidence
seat record: retired-gap-duration-ratio-20260915T0740Z.json
Result in full
The frozen criterion required the DURATION-WEIGHTED contested figure under RETIRES-EVERYTHING to be at or below 7,452.9 us per step. Measured 6,180.1 us, so SUPPORTED. MEASURED: mean gap 49.8641 us over all 7,437.7 gaps per step; mean gap 57.8055 us over the 3,446.0 elementwise-FOLLOWED gaps; RATIO 1.1593. Duration-weighted contention 5,974.9 us under RETIRES-NOTHING (stack 56,064.7, clears by 1,478.0) and 6,180.1 us under RETIRES-EVERYTHING (stack 55,859.5, clears by 1,272.9). The ratio would have to reach about 1.406 to refute; it is 1.159, so the verdict has about 21 percent of ratio headroom. THE DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT I PRE-STATED, AND THAT IS THE RESULT WORTH REPORTING. The docstring predicted a ratio BELOW 1.0 on the reasoning that clustered small kernels are what fusion targets and a kernel inside a dense launch cluster sits closer to its neighbour. The retiring gaps are LONGER on the mean, so cycle 40 count-share figure of 5,154.1 us UNDERSTATED the contention by about 820 us and cycle 40 worst-case margin drops from 2,093.7 us to 1,272.9 us. The composition still clears 1.5x under the hostile reading, which is what the criterion asked, but it clears by less than the predecessor said and the correction again runs against the direction that flatters me. THE MEAN AND THE MEDIAN DISAGREE IN SIGN, which is why both were published before the run. Median gap 19.4570 us over all gaps against 16.5752 us over the retiring ones, a median ratio of 0.852: the TYPICAL retiring gap is shorter, exactly as predicted, while the MEAN retiring gap is longer because a tail of long holes sits adjacent to elementwise kernels. Both are true and only the mean is the correct weight for this arithmetic, because a total equals a count times a MEAN -- so the verdict uses 1.1593 and the median is reported as the distributional finding rather than as an alternative number. THE REFUSAL WAS PROVED BEFORE THE GREEN RUN: --prove-red blanks the elementwise selector and the script exits 2 rather than publishing a zero or undefined ratio, reporting 44,626 gaps total so the trace and window scoping are known good.
Limitations, and what this does not close
A SHARPENING THAT RUNS AGAINST THIS VERDICT AND WAS NOT IN THE PRE-REGISTERED CAVEATS. The uniformity argument models the profiler as adding a fixed cost c per launch boundary to BOTH populations. Under that model the observed ratio is (m_e + c) / (m_a + c), which is pulled TOWARD 1.0 from whichever side it starts on. An observed ratio ABOVE 1.0 therefore cannot have been manufactured by additive uniform inflation out of a true ratio below 1.0, and the true ratio must be HIGHER than the measured 1.1593, not lower. So the additive model makes this measurement CONSERVATIVE in the direction that hurts: the real contention is at least 6,180.1 us and plausibly more, and the real margin is at most 1,272.9 us. The measurement cannot bound c from this trace, so no corrected number is published -- what is published is the sign of the bias, which is the part that matters for whether the verdict is safe. It is safe by 1,272.9 us with the bias pointing the wrong way and about 21 percent of ratio headroom before the flip. THE TWO PRE-REGISTERED WAYS THE UNIFORMITY ARGUMENT CAN FAIL STAND UNCHECKED, and neither is checkable from this trace: (1) if the profiler per-boundary cost SCALES with kernel duration rather than being fixed per launch it does not divide out at all, and the argument above about the sign of the bias goes with it; (2) if retiring kernels cluster near window edges or host synchronisation their gaps carry a different kind of time than a mid-chain gap and the ratio is not a clean correction. The mean/median sign split is direct evidence that the retiring population is NOT a uniformly rescaled copy of the whole, which makes (2) more live than it was before this run, not less: something is putting long holes next to elementwise kernels and nothing here says what. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE. The governed-basis gap-duration measurement remains OWED. This cycle refines the number by measuring a ratio within one profiled trace; it does not settle the durations, and the separation clause still forbids composing absolute profiled durations with a governed figure. The optimizer share is NOT ratio-corrected because nothing measures that population own duration ratio; leaving it at the count share is conservative only if the optimizer population is not itself long-tailed, which is unmeasured. ALSO STILL OPEN AND NOW THE BINDING WEAKNESS: all three levers remain MAXIMAL-EFFECTIVENESS ceilings rather than measured effects, so any arm this stack licenses is licensed on ceilings. No matched-run variation exists for any of it, so the governed-run evidence contract repeatability clause stays unsatisfied. Cycles 38 through 41 have now spent four cycles refining one correction term whose total movement is about 1,026 us of a 62,039.6 us stack; the contention question is closed and the ceiling-versus-measured-effect question is where the next cycle belongs.

The idle lever prices idle it cannot reach dependency bound holesdiagnostic, existing captureEvery device event in the trace carries a correlation id linking it to the host launch call that issued it.The frozen criterion said REFUTED IF the DEPENDENCY hole COUNT share, on whichever population is most favourable to the composition, EXCEEDS 0.0480.REFUTEDWHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and the not-closed half is larger than the refutation.
Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
REFUTED IF the DEPENDENCY hole COUNT share, on whichever of the two populations is most favourable to the composition, EXCEEDS 0.0480 -- equivalently if the three-lever stack falls below 54,586.7 us per step once the idle lever is scaled to the holes it can actually reach. THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE BAR AND FROM NOTHING READ IN ANY RECEIPT: 1.5x on the 0.16376 s governed step needs 54,586.7 us removed; the elementwise and optimizer levers supply 29,339.6 us between them; cycle 41 measured the contested overlap at 0.18899 of whatever the idle lever is, so the idle lever must supply 25,247.1 / 0.81101 = 31,130.2 us of reachable idle out of its priced 32,700.0, which is 95.2% of it. Any dependency share above 4.80% therefore refutes. ALSO REFUTED, independently of any share, IF THE CORRELATION JOIN FAILS: the instrument exits non-zero when every hole is UNATTRIBUTED, or when more than 10% of holes are, rather than publishing a dependency share of zero -- because a zero would read as "no idle is dependency-bound", hand the idle lever its full 32,700.0 us, and be indistinguishable in arithmetic from a broken join. I EXPECT THIS TO REFUTE, and I am saying so before the run rather than after, because I have already read the split receipt's hole counts. That is exactly why the threshold above is computed from the bar rather than chosen, and why the verdict binds on the population most favourable to the thing I expect to refute.
Instrument

Evidence
seat record: idle-lever-dependency-floor-20260915T0825Z.json
Result in full
The frozen criterion said REFUTED IF the DEPENDENCY hole COUNT share, on whichever population is most favourable to the composition, EXCEEDS 0.0480. Measured 0.3642 on the favourable population and 0.3677 on the other -- SEVEN AND A HALF TIMES the threshold, so REFUTED, and not marginally. MEASURED, over 6 windows: on the all-device population, 7,906.7 interior holes per step of which DEPENDENCY_HOST_BUSY 2,766.7 and DEPENDENCY_HOST_IDLE 113.3 against HOST_DISPATCH 5,026.7; on the kernel-only population that cycles 38-41 priced, 7,437.7 holes of which 2,625.7 + 109.5 dependency against 4,702.5 host-dispatch. Both populations agree to within 0.0035 of each other, so the answer does not turn on which one the 32,700.0 us figure covers. THE ARITHMETIC IT FORCES: the idle lever can reach 20,789.0 us of its priced 32,700.0; re-applying cycle 41 measured contested share of 0.18899 to the smaller lever gives 3,928.9 us contested; the three-lever stack becomes 46,199.7 us against a 54,586.7 us requirement, SHORT BY 8,386.9 us. On the 0.16376 s governed step that stack is about 1.393x, below the 1.5x floor that 1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1 requires before any arm may be dispatched. THE COUNT AND THE DURATION DISAGREE BY MORE THAN AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE and the disagreement is the evidence, not a problem: dependency is 36.4% of holes by COUNT and 2.3% by profiled DURATION, because the profiler inflates exactly the host-side time that HOST_DISPATCH holes are made of. Count survives profiling, duration does not -- the principle cycles 38-41 established, pointing the other way here. Anyone reading the duration share would conclude the idle lever is almost entirely reachable, and that reading is an artifact of the instrument. THE BIAS RUNS AGAINST THE REFUTATION, which is the direction that makes it safe to act on: profiling lengthens every launch call, so a launch that truly returned before a hole can appear still-open and be misclassified as HOST_DISPATCH, never the reverse. 0.3642 is a LOWER BOUND on the true dependency share and 46,199.7 us is an UPPER BOUND on the stack. I PREDICTED THIS REFUTATION IN WRITING BEFORE THE RUN, and disclosed in the same breath that I had already read the prior split receipt hole counts -- which is why the threshold was computed from the bar (54,586.7 needed, 29,339.6 from the other two levers, cycle 41 contested share) rather than chosen, and why the verdict binds on the population most favourable to the thing I expected to refute. The deliberate red was proved first: dropping every launch correlation makes all 44,626 holes UNATTRIBUTED and the script exits 2 rather than publishing a dependency share of zero, which would have handed the idle lever its full 32,700.0 us.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and the not-closed half is larger than the refutation. A DEPENDENCY hole is NOT unreachable idle. It is idle unreachable by THIS lever as priced -- the launch-rate lever, which makes launches cheaper or fewer. The device sitting idle with its next kernel already issued is the definition of work serialized behind other work, and that is precisely the population the whole-step graph with the optimizer on a second stream targets. That is row 3 of the factor-dominant table (~32 ms, 19% of the 4x), it is one of the two rows nobody has touched, and it is a SEPARATE lever that this cycle has just SIZED rather than retired: 2,880.0 holes per step, 36.4% of all interior holes, with their durations unmeasured on any governed basis. So the honest reading is not that the idle is gone, it is that the idle was assigned to the wrong lever. WHAT IT DOES CLOSE. The three-lever composition -- idle + elementwise + optimizer -- does not reach 1.5x. It reaches about 1.393x on the governed step under the most favourable population, with the measurement bias pointing further down. WHAT IS NOW UNVERIFIED AND WAS NOT BEFORE. The other two levers have had no such audit. The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF the unreachable charge on the ISOLATED set EXCEEDS 7,452.9 us per step -- the margin the composition ever had, computed from the bar in cycle 38 and reused unchanged through 39, 40 and 41. Measured 4,141.1 us per step, which is 55.6% of that threshold, so the criterion is met and the verdict is SUPPORTED. THE PARTITION. Of 3,447.0 elementwise kernels per step holding 27,447.4 us of device time, 2,700.0 kernels (20,840.1 us device, 14,479.6 us credited) have at least one in-class device neighbour and so have a candidate fusible edge; 747.0 kernels (6,607.3 us device, 4,625.9 us credited) have neither device neighbour in the class, so no fusion within this class can hold their intermediate in a register. Charging those isolated kernels only their eliminable-byte credit and letting them keep min(dur, excess) gives the 4,141.1 us. Isolated kernels are 21.67% of the class by count and carry 24.21% of its credited time. THE LEVER WAS RECOMPUTED, NOT ASSUMED: the capped composite from the inherited byte model comes out at 19,105.6 us per step against the 19,105.6 us the composition prices, with the two halves at 7,017.0 excess and 13,703.8 eliminable-byte pre-cap and sized coverage 0.9960. The audit therefore describes the same lever the composition uses, to the last microsecond. SUPPORTED IS ABOUT THE LEVER AND NOT ABOUT THE COMPOSITION, and the composition moved the other way. The elementwise lever falls from 19,105.6 to 14,964.5 us and the three-lever stack falls from cycle 42's 46,199.7 to 42,058.6 us against the 54,586.7 required -- short by 12,528.1 us, about 1.346x on the 0.16376 s governed step. Cycle 42 already ruled that composition REFUTED; this cycle lowers it further and rules only that the remaining shortfall is not attributable to the adjacency half of this lever's premise. THE BIAS RUNS THE SAME WAY IT DID IN CYCLE 42. Adjacency over-counts fusibility, because two adjacent elementwise kernels need not be dataflow-connected. So GROUPED is an upper bound on the genuinely fusible set, 4,141.1 us is a LOWER bound on the unreachable credit, and 14,964.5 us is an UPPER bound on the audited lever. A SUPPORTED verdict computed from a lower bound on the damage is the weaker direction of this instrument, and that is stated rather than glossed.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, and the largest item is bigger than what the cycle settled. (1) THE EXCESS HALF IS A ONE-SIDED RESIDUAL AND IS UNAUDITED. 7,017.0 us of the lever is sum over kernels of max(0, dur - bytes_time) at a PUBLISHED 1008.0 GB/s reference. The clamp is per kernel, so a kernel faster than the reference contributes 0 rather than a negative, while a slower one contributes its full shortfall. The class as a whole achieves 1073.6 GB/s -- ABOVE the reference -- so the two-sided aggregate residual is negative and 7,017.0 us is the sum of one tail of a distribution straddling zero. Whether that tail is removable overhead or is kernels whose working set exceeds the 72 MB L2 is unmeasured, and it is the named successor. (2) REGISTER AND SHARED-MEMORY CAPACITY IS STILL ENTIRELY UNMEASURED, and adjacency does not touch it. A GROUPED kernel whose intermediate is a [4096, 32768] tensor is 256 MiB at bf16; nothing holds that in registers, so having an in-class neighbour is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. The 14,479.6 us credited to grouped kernels is bounded by this cycle from below only. (3) NO DATAFLOW EDGE IS PROVEN. Adjacency on the device timeline is a proxy; the trace carries no producer-consumer relation between tensors. (4) THE OPTIMIZER LEVER, 10,234.0 us, has had no ceiling audit at all. It is distance to a bandwidth floor computed under the same published rate this cycle just found the elementwise excess half resting on, so the two share a premise. (5) The three levers are still priced against ONE capture, one process, under profiling instrumentation, with no matched-run variation -- so under the governed-run evidence contract none of them is quotable as a measured ceiling for a governed run. WHAT THE CYCLE ALSO CORRECTED, recorded because it is a correction of my own published prose rather than of an instrument. The cycle-42 ledger block asked whether the 19,105.6 us figure "already contains launch/idle time the idle lever ALSO counts". Reading the source settles it: the per-kernel credit is min(dur_us, excess + eliminable_byte_time) summed over kernel DEVICE durations, so no host time and no inter-kernel hole can enter it. The same block quoted "16.3 us per removed kernel ... far above a typical elementwise kernel's device time" as an anomaly; that divided the whole lever by only the fully-removed count. The receipt's own split is 1,172.3 kernels removed outright for 8,634.1 us, or 7.365 us each, which is entirely ordinary. There was no anomaly and the sentence should not have been published.

The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF the one-sided excess sitting on DRAM_BOUND kernels -- those whose sized working set exceeds the 72 MB L2 -- EXCEEDS 4,730.5 us per step, the difference between the elementwise lever after cycle 43 (14,964.5) and the optimizer lever (10,234.0), because a double count above that inverts the campaign's own ranking of the two audited levers. Measured 151.2 us per step, 3.2% of the threshold and 2.2% of the 7,017.0 us excess half. The criterion is met and the verdict is SUPPORTED. THE PARTITION. Only 8.0 of 3,447.0 elementwise kernels per step have a sized working set above L2. They hold 3,469.8 us of device time -- 12.6% of the class -- and carry just 151.2 us of the one-sided excess, because they are the large aten::copy_ and aten::fill_ sites that already run near or above the published rate. The other 3,439.0 kernels fit in L2 and carry 6,865.8 us of the excess. So the mechanism I proposed is not what is behind the excess half: the double count of DRAM traffic exists and is 151.2 us, which is not material to anything. THE ONE-SIDED READING REPRODUCED THE PRICED FIGURE EXACTLY -- 7,017.0 us against the 7,017.0 us the composition spends, at sized coverage 0.9960 -- so the instrument is auditing the same quantity and not a neighbour of it. SUPPORTED HERE MEANS THE PROPOSED MECHANISM FAILED, NOT THAT THE ESTIMATOR IS SOUND. The cycle measured something larger than its own criterion and that finding is recorded in the update, unruled, because a verdict re-cut to fit numbers already in hand is chosen to fit them. The elementwise lever moves only 14,964.5 -> 14,813.3 us and the three-lever stack 42,058.6 -> 41,907.4 us against 54,586.7 needed, which changes no ranking and revives no composition.
Limitations, and what this does not close
THE FINDING THIS CYCLE PRODUCED OUTSIDE ITS OWN CRITERION, AND IT IS LARGER THAN THE ONE IT RULED. The three readings of the estimator are: one-sided at the published rate +7,017.0 us per step; TWO-sided at the same rate MINUS 1,668.5 us per step; one-sided at the class's own measured 1073.6 GB/s +7,548.0 us, two-sided there +110.1 us. Per step 2,253.3 kernels carry a positive residual and 1,193.7 a negative one. So the per-kernel residual is a distribution centred within about 110 us of zero once the reference is the class's own rate, and the 7,017.0 us the composition spends is the positive half of it. That is DISPERSION, not a systematic shortfall, and the per-kernel clamp is what converts one into the other: it manufactures an 8,685.5 us difference between the one-sided and two-sided readings of the same population. WHY THAT IS NOT RULED HERE. The frozen criterion asked whether DRAM traffic explains the excess. It does not, by 151.2 us. Ruling the dispersion finding under this cycle would be choosing a criterion after seeing the numbers, so it is recorded and named as the successor instead: whether the positive dispersion is collectible at all, or whether a kernel slower than its class mean is simply a different shape or dtype with a genuinely lower achievable rate, which no fusion collects. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. (1) The dispersion question above, which is 7,017.0 us of a 14,813.3 us lever -- 47% of it. (2) THE L2 TEST IS A WORKING-SET TEST, NOT A RESIDENCY MEASUREMENT: no L2 hit-rate counter exists in this build, a kernel under 72 MB can miss L2 because it shares the cache with everything in flight, and a kernel above it can hit on part of its traffic. The two errors run opposite ways and I cannot sign the net, which is why this cycle carries no one-directional bias argument where cycles 42 and 43 both did. (3) Register and shared-memory capacity remains entirely unmeasured, so cycle 43's 14,479.6 us credited to grouped kernels is still bounded from below only. (4) THE OPTIMIZER LEVER, 10,234.0 us, still has had no audit, and it is distance to a bandwidth floor computed under this same published rate -- which this cycle has now shown the class as a whole EXCEEDS by 6.5%, so the optimizer figure inherits the question directly. (5) One capture, one process, under profiling instrumentation, no matched-run variation.

Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THIS RETIRES, AND IT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE RETIREMENT OF THE AUDIT. A fusion collects between-site heterogeneity only by changing the shapes, and changing the shapes is exactly what the BYTE half of this same lever prices -- 13,703.8 us of eliminable intermediate traversals. Crediting the between-site excess as well charges the same mechanism twice, which is the double count the per-kernel cap in the original instrument was written to prevent and did not catch, because the cap bounds a kernel against its own duration and cannot see that its two halves name one act. So 5,697.9 us/step comes off: elementwise lever 14,813.3 -> 9,115.4 us/step; three-lever stack 41,907.4 -> 36,209.5 of the 54,586.7 required, short by 18,377.2, about 1.28x. THE RANKING FLIPS, WHICH IS WHAT THE THRESHOLD WAS FOR. The elementwise lever now stands BELOW the optimizer lever (9,115.4 against 10,234.0) for the first time in this campaign. Three cycles ago it was 19,105.6 and was the largest of the three. A DEFECT IN MY OWN FROZEN CRITERION, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY PASSED. I froze the threshold against the SURVIVING within-site residual and labelled it "the threshold that reorders the two levers". The quantity that actually reorders them is the RETIRED amount, so the exact flip condition is within-site < 2,437.7 us/step, not <= 4,579.3. The two are not the same number and I wrote them as though they were. The measured 1,319.1 clears BOTH readings, so the verdict and the reordering both stand on the arithmetic rather than on the looser wording -- but a criterion whose stated meaning and stated number disagree is a defect even when the result is insensitive to it, and it would not have been insensitive at 3,000 us. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS NOT CLOSED. The 1,319.1 us/step of within-site dispersion is NOT established as removable overhead and this cycle does not claim it is. Scheduling, clock and power state, L2 occupancy from neighbouring work, and measurement noise all produce within-site dispersion, and no counter in this build separates them from per-kernel launch cost. The number bounds where overhead COULD live -- 1,319.1 us/step, 4.8% of the class device time -- and nothing more. Also untouched: sites are keyed on recorded input dims, so two genuinely different workloads sharing a dims string merge into one site and inflate the within-site figure, which means the true within-site dispersion is at or below 1,319.1 and the retirement is if anything understated. THE SUCCESSOR IS THE OPTIMIZER LEVER AND IT INHERITS THIS EXACT QUESTION. 10,234.0 us is the last of the three with no audit at all, and it is distance to a bandwidth floor computed under the same published 1008.0 GB/s reference that this class exceeds by 6.5%. A floor computed under a rate the hardware beats is not a floor, and after this cycle it is also the LARGEST remaining lever.

The class figure is dragged down by SMALL movement kernels where launch cost dominates the duration, and the calibration set deliberately excluded exactly those. So the direction of my prediction survived and its mechanism did not, and a prediction whose reasoning fails is a prediction that got lucky. THE FINDING IS LARGER THAN THE VERDICT AND IT POINTS AT THE BYTE MODEL. A measured achieved rate of 1240.7 GB/s is 23% ABOVE this card's published peak, on kernels selected precisely because their working set exceeds L2 and their byte accounting is the least arguable in the class. A rate above the physical peak is not a fast kernel; it is an arithmetic that has attributed more bytes to a kernel than the kernel moved, or traffic that was served from cache despite a working set larger than the cache. Either reading is a defect in the DERIVED byte model, and that model is not a detail of this cycle -- it is what produced the 13,703.8 us eliminable-bytes half of the elementwise lever, the single largest quantity in the entire audit. SO THIS CYCLE DOES NOT BANK ITS OWN NUMBER. 11,468.8 us is a LARGER lever than the priced 10,234.0 and therefore the more favourable figure for the campaign, and it rests on a reference rate this same cycle has just found reason to distrust. The optimizer lever stays at 10,234.0 pending the byte-model audit, and the three-lever stack stays at 36,209.5 of the 54,586.7 required. Adopting a favourable number computed on a basis I have just impeached would be the exact move the campaign has been correcting for three days. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, AND ONE PIECE OF IT SPANS THE THRESHOLD. The reference set's rates run from 798.6 to 1240.7 GB/s and the rate at which the two levers swap places is 861.6 GB/s, so a reference drawn from the low end of the observed spread -- or from the whole pure-movement class at 778.4 -- would have produced SUPPORTED. The frozen criterion named max and median, both landed on the same side, and the verdict follows the criterion as frozen; the sensitivity is recorded here UNRULED rather than used to re-cut the verdict after the numbers were in. Also untouched: no MEASURED device-memory traffic exists for any kernel in this campaign, so both the optimizer footprint and the calibration bytes are derived quantities that the governed-run evidence contract requires to be reported separately from measured traffic; and the optimizer is a multi-tensor kernel walking 702 moment tensors rather than a contiguous copy, so if its access pattern is less efficient than the calibration set's its true floor is HIGHER and its true lever SMALLER than any reading here. THE SUCCESSOR IS THE BYTE MODEL ITSELF, and it is the first cycle of this audit that attacks a quantity rather than a lever: whether the derived byte accounting over-counts, established by the fact that it yields achieved rates above the card's physical peak, and by how much.

Limitations, and what this does not close
THE BOUND FALSIFIES A CONJUNCTION AND THE HYPOTHESIS NAMED ONLY ONE OF ITS TERMS. The ceiling assumes three things at once: the byte count is right, the kernel duration is right, and 1008.0 GB/s is this card's peak. Exceeding it falsifies their conjunction, not any single term. My hypothesis named the byte model, the criterion was frozen on it, and the verdict follows the criterion -- but the artifact does not get to convert that into a proof that bytes are the guilty term, and this update says so before anything downstream quotes it. THE MAGNITUDE POINTS AWAY FROM THE BYTES, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE. To bring 1240.7 under its 1084.2 ceiling the byte count would have to be inflated by a factor of 1.144. A byte model that miscounts traversals is wrong by a WHOLE TRAVERSAL -- 2x, 1.5x, 1.33x for two, three or four traversals counted as one more or one fewer. There is no traversal arithmetic that produces 14.4%. So the shape of the error does not look like the mechanism my own hypothesis named, and the term that would explain it cleanly is the REFERENCE: if this card sustains more than 1240.7 GB/s on a 1 GiB device-to-device copy, every one of these kernels is innocent and so is the byte model, and what is wrong is the specification figure the whole campaign divides by. WHY THAT IS NOT A LOOPHOLE I GET TO TAKE TODAY. 1008.0 GB/s is what a 384-bit bus at 21 Gbps yields, and a sustained rate 23% above it is not something a memory controller does. The remaining candidates are memory compression on the copy path, a duration that the profiler under-reports for these specific kernels, or dims that over-state the tensor -- and this cycle distinguishes none of them. What it establishes is that the three terms cannot all be right, which was not established before and which every lever in this campaign depends on. I PREDICTED REFUTED AND THE MEASUREMENT WENT THE OTHER WAY, at more than six times the threshold. My registered basis was that the large copies would be small enough for cache to explain -- I put the break-even at about 384 MiB and expected the trace's copies to sit under it. They are 1 GiB, nearly three times that size, and I had the trace on disk when I wrote the prediction. That is a guess where a lookup was available, which is the failure my own standing rule names, and the second cycle running where my reasoning was wrong: cycle 46 got the direction right for the wrong reason, this one got the direction wrong outright. Both generative, both mine. NOTHING IS RESTATED. No lever moves on this cycle. The elementwise lever stays 9,115.4, the optimizer 10,234.0, the stack 36,209.5 of 54,586.7. A finding that three terms cannot all be right does not tell me which figure to change, and changing one before knowing would be worse than leaving them.

READ THE HYPOTHESIS ID AGAINST THE VERDICT BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. This cycle inherited cycle 47's successor id, which asserts that the over-peak copies impeach the REFERENCE RATE and not the byte count. The criterion frozen at PREDICT is the opposite proposition -- SUPPORTED means the recorded operands justify a smaller byte figure, so the BYTE MODEL is the guilty term -- and the loop rules on the frozen criterion, not on the label. THE CORRECTION IS 4/3 AND IT IS A DTYPE-WIDTH RATIO, NOT A TRAVERSAL RATIO. bytes_corrected charges a movement op TRUE_TRAVERSALS[op] * max(sizes) -- twice the LARGEST operand for a copy. That is exact for a same-dtype copy, where source and destination are the same size. It over-charges whenever the operands differ, which is exactly what a converting copy is, and the over-charge is 2*max/(max+min) = 2*4/(4+2) = 4/3 for an fp32/bf16 pair. CYCLE 47'S MAGNITUDE ARGUMENT FOUND THE RIGHT NUMBER AND THE WRONG MECHANISM, AND THAT IS THE GENERALISABLE PART. It reasoned that bringing 1240.7 under 1084.2 needs 1.144, that a traversal miscount is wrong by a whole traversal -- it listed 2x, 1.5x and 1.33x explicitly -- and that no traversal arithmetic yields 14.4%, therefore the bytes were probably innocent. The available correction turned out to be 1.333, one of the three ratios it named, arriving by a mechanism it had not considered: operand WIDTH, not traversal COUNT. The inference "the required factor is not a ratio my mechanism produces, so my mechanism is not the culprit" silently assumes the mechanism list is complete. A required factor of 1.144 is a LOWER BOUND on the correction needed, never a target to match, and 1.333 clears it with room. I PREDICTED REFUTED AND I WAS WRONG FOR THE THIRD CYCLE RUNNING, AND THIS ONE IS THE WORST OF THE THREE. Cycle 46 was right for the wrong reason, cycle 47 was wrong outright from a guess where a lookup was available, and I wrote in this cycle's own prediction that its basis was "a SOURCE READ rather than a guess".
