It said nothing about what the operands ARE, and I closed that gap with "I expect them to match" while the dims and dtypes sat in the same trace the instrument was about to read. A half-lookup presented as a lookup is worse than an admitted guess, because it carries the authority of the half that was checked. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, AND NO LEVER MOVES ON IT. The 13,703.8 us eliminable-bytes half of the elementwise lever is computed by this same formula and is therefore under suspicion, but suspicion is not a restatement: correcting it needs the class-wide share of unequal-operand kernels, which is the successor. Elementwise stays 9,115.4, optimizer 10,234.0, stack 36,209.5 of 54,586.7.

(3) ARITHMETIC, SIZED, ABOVE THE REFERENCE RATE -- 1,824 kernels, 1,416.7 us/step. SUPPORTED against the frozen criterion, and the source says it plainly. ember_v0_document_reduction.py:93-94 at head 20338ddc are the body of reduce_weight_gradient, whose loop header at line 92 is "for start, end in document_spans(lengths, order)". Line 93 allocates one partial per DOCUMENT -- upstream[start:end].transpose(0, 1) @ values[start:end], one document dY^T @ X at the weight shape -- and line 94 allocates the running total of the same shape. Neither loop in the enclosing chain iterates over parameters, gradients or leaves, so the refutation clause did not fire; both lines bind the result of an out-of-place operator, so the second clause did not fire either. The three distinct allocation sizes the census found are therefore three WEIGHT SHAPES reduced through this function, not three leaf classes, and the 255.3 allocations per step are documents times reduced linears -- a quantity with no leaf term in it at all. INSTRUMENT DEFECT, found by running it and repaired once: the first allocation detector listed named constructors only and classed "a.transpose(0,1) @ b" and "total + partial" as non-allocating, which would have refuted on clause 2 while looking at two expressions that each allocate an output tensor. The repair adds out-of-place operators whose result is bound to a name -- a fact about torch, not about this file -- and the deliberate red still fires on an import line under the wider detector.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND WHAT IT OPENS. (1) It closes the ALLOCATION route for naming individual leaves at the reduction: this site cannot carry a per-leaf key at any granularity, size or volume, because it never allocates per leaf. It does NOT close the 72-unstepped-leaf question, which now has to be answered structurally from the parameter registry or from a non-allocation key, not from allocator provenance. It is NOT a free win and must not be filed as one -- the function docstring states that nothing is promoted to a wider accumulator because matching the reference means matching its rounding, and the reduction ORDER is an argument, so any batching is contract-touching and owes an equivalence proof before it is a candidate. REFUTED against the frozen criterion at clause 1, and the cause is MY OWN GROUP SELECTOR, which is stated first because the numbers underneath it happen to favour the proposition and reading them as a verdict would be fitting a conclusion to data already on disk. The criterion read: "(1) AGREEMENT WITH THE PRIOR INSTRUMENTS: the in-group add total is not 2,178, or the out-of-group total is not 288, or the number of groups carrying adds is not 726." Measured: in-group 2,160, outside 306, groups 726. The group count agrees exactly; the two totals are off by 18 in opposite directions, so 18 adds moved from in-group to outside. THE 18 ARE NAMED BY THE INSTRUMENT OWN OUTPUT: the outside leading-shape histogram reads 4096x1024 x288 and 32768x1024 x18 -- three adds in each of the six instances, at exactly the shape the predecessor cycle proved is the real dW. THE DEFECT: to build the corrected group set this instrument had to drop the dX group in each of the six, and the rule it used was "the group whose output leading dimension is another group contracted dimension, and whose two output dimensions differ". That rule is SYMMETRIC in its first half -- both groups satisfy it -- so the second half is an arbitrary tiebreak, and the tiebreak selected the [32768,1024] group, which is the dW. It deleted the weight-gradient loop and kept the activation gradient. THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT THE PREVIOUS CYCLE REFUTED ON, reproduced one cycle later in a different place, after I had named the repaired asymmetric discriminator in that cycle not_closed list and then did not use it. WHAT HELD, AND IT IS THE PROPOSITION SUBSTANCE: clause 2 HELD -- all 2,160 in-group adds carry two readable two-dimensional operands. CLAUSE 3 HELD WITH ZERO FAILURES ACROSS THE WHOLE POPULATION -- operands equal 2,160, operands differing 0, and the op name histogram is aten::add x2,160 and nothing else. So there is no broadcast add, no bias add, no in-place add against a differently shaped operand, and no foreach add anywhere in the population: every accumulation add the deficit cycle admitted on its first operand alone is in fact a genuine two-operand partial sum at its group weight output shape. That was the specific weakness this cycle was opened to test and it is answered. AN OBSERVATION, NOT A VERDICT: the distribution reads 720 groups at exactly 3 adds and 6 groups at 0, and 720 x 3 = 2,160 plus the six 18 misplaced adds = 2,178 over 726 groups, which is the forced three-per-group distribution. The criterion failed before that could be read as a finding, so it is recorded as what the repaired successor is expected to confirm rather than as what this cycle showed.
Limitations, and what this does not close
(1) THE REPAIRED DISCRIMINATOR IS NOW OVERDETERMINED AND STILL HAS NOT RUN. It was named one cycle ago -- a genuine dW loop combines its partials by ADDITION at the weight shape, a dX loop by CONCATENATION -- and this cycle own outside histogram supplies the evidence directly: the eighteen displaced adds sit at 32768x1024, so the group whose output shape matches the add operand shapes is the dW. That rule is asymmetric by construction and needs no tiebreak. Two consecutive refutations now point at it. (2) THE DEFECT CLASS IS MINE AND IS WORTH A RULE, NOT A RESOLUTION TO BE MORE CAREFUL. Both refusals came from a symmetric test with an arbitrary tiebreak standing in for an asymmetric fact I already held. The generalisable form: when two candidates satisfy a test equally, a tiebreak added to break the symmetry is a GUESS wearing the test grammar, and the fix is always to find the fact that distinguishes them rather than to order them. (3) NOTHING IS ESTABLISHED ABOUT THE SIX ADDS THEMSELVES BEYOND THEIR SHAPE. They were counted as outside-group here, which is an artefact of the selector, so their per-group distribution inside the six is confirmed only by the predecessor cycle reading of three adds per instance. (4) NOTHING ABOUT TIME. Call classification and operand shapes only: no timing claim, no saving, no ceiling, no candidate. (5) One profiled trace, 6 measured steps, recorded input dims only, no matched-run variation, no measured device traffic, no occupancy counter. Measured: 0.0000 over zero calls. Neither branch describes what happened, and taking the SUPPORTED branch on the arithmetic alone would publish the sentence the hypothesis actually asserts -- that the arm reaches a row-sized share -- which is FALSE. There is no share to size. The hypothesis PRESUPPOSED an installable arm and that presupposition is refuted at the source: install_fp8_up_gate_projections raises on exactly-14-decoder-layers before it examines a single shape and CIA-3B has 24, then DynamicFp8UpGateProjection._shape_holds requires a weight of [8H,H] while the CIA-3B shared_ffn.up_gate is [2048,1024] at hidden_size 1024 and shared_ffn_dim 2048 in the config the checkpoint manifest binds by digest. The mechanism half of the hypothesis stands and is confirmed from source -- _DynamicFp8ScaledMm.backward runs both dX and dW through .to(weight.dtype) on a master weight the installer requires to be bfloat16, so the arm is FORWARD-ONLY and could never exceed the 0.3334 forward share even where it does install. I take REFUTED rather than the flattering branch because my own record says both of my errors on an unwanted result ran favourable, and this outcome is worse for the route than either branch I wrote.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, and the list is longer than what it closes. (1) FP8 AS A ROUTE IS UNTOUCHED. What is refuted is that a usable implementation already exists for the canonical architecture. The machinery does exist and is reusable: DynamicFp8Projection, the torch._scaled_mm dispatch, the arm switch, the dispatch receipt, the post-optimizer refresh, the SM89 layout check, and the #2173 per-tensor encoding that folds both scales into the kernel epilogue and removes the separate output rescale pass -- which is the cure for the wrapper cost the prior decomposition measured at 586.875 us, of which the unfused abs+reduce amax pair alone was 346.590. THREE CONSTANTS bind it to the wrong model: _FP8_W5_LAYER_COUNT 14 against 24 decoder layers, DynamicFp8UpGateProjection._shape_holds at 8H against a 2H shared_ffn, and DynamicFp8DownProjection._shape_holds at 4H against a 3072 expert_ffn_dim which is 3H. Those are ratio constants, not a rewrite. (2) THE MEASURED STEP'S OWN SITES ARE SIZED AND UNADDRESSED: contractions at the CIA shared-FFN width carry 0.2712 of leaf arithmetic, the vocabulary projection at 1024-to-32768 carries 0.0452 over 6 forward calls, and neither has ever had an FP8 arm pointed at it. (3) THE FORWARD-ONLY LIMIT IS THE STRUCTURAL ONE AND IT IS ARCHITECTURE-INDEPENDENT: _DynamicFp8ScaledMm.backward computes both dX and dW in the master dtype, so even a correctly-shaped arm caps at the 0.3334 forward share, and two thirds of the arithmetic is out of its reach by construction. An FP8 BACKWARD is a new mechanism, not an overlooked one, and it is where the remaining arithmetic lives. (4) FP16 ACCUMULATION carries the same published dense rate on this card, is not shape-bound in the same way, and nothing here speaks to it. (5) THE #1413 MATCHED-LOSS BAR IS UNCHANGED; the W5 canary cleared it at worst relative 1.169e-3 against a 1e-2 limit, but it cleared it on the 14-layer 8H model, so that adjudication does not transfer to CIA-3B any more than the installer does. (6) NO CEILING IS COMPOSED and no arm is proposed. The instrument refused to compose one and that refusal is the finding.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
FROZEN BEFORE ANY TRACE IS READ FOR THIS CYCLE. UNIT OF COMPARISON is a GROUP keyed by (trace, kernel symbol, grid dimensions, block dimensions) so a symbol launched at two different geometries is never compared against itself across them -- shape is the obvious confound and it is excluded by the key rather than by hope. PREDICTOR is not the immediately preceding gap, because clock and thermal state have a millisecond time constant and a microsecond gap cannot move it: for each invocation compute the DEVICE BUSY FRACTION over the 5,000 us of trace immediately preceding its start, as union-of-device-intervals clipped to that window divided by 5,000. BUCKETS with an explicit margin and an excluded middle, per a-strict-order-clause-meets-a-tie clause 3: LOW is busy fraction below 0.40, HIGH is above 0.90, and every invocation between them is EXCLUDED and counted in the residual rather than assigned. SCOREABILITY, frozen: a group scores only with at least 30 invocations in EACH bucket. The test runs on BOTH traces because the eager trace at 0.227 coverage supplies the low-density population the captured trace at 0.843 may not have, and the verdict uses the POOLED invocation-weighted mean of per-group ratio mean_HIGH/mean_LOW with per-trace figures reported beside it. SUPPORTED IF the pooled weighted mean ratio is at least 1.05 AND at least two thirds of scoreable groups individually exceed 1.00 -- duration rises with sustained device load, the inflation is physical, the captured durations are the faithful ones and the eager total was an underestimate. REFUTED IF the pooled weighted mean ratio is below 1.05 -- duration is flat against load, the load explanation fails, and instrumentation returns as the leading explanation for the 1.2889x, which would mean every captured-priced lever is overstated and the 1.6940x arm falls below the 1.5x bar. INCONCLUSIVE IF fewer than three groups are scoreable, or if the scoreable groups carry less than 0.30 of the pooled device sum. COUNTER-EVIDENCE CLAUSE, per a-strict-order-clause clause 4: any scoreable group whose ratio points the other way is NAMED in the ruling with its numbers, never absorbed into the weighted mean. RESIDUAL per an-op-name-filter-is-a-classifier: the instrument reports, as first-class numbers, the excluded-middle invocation count and device-time share, the unscoreable-group count and share, and the count of groups that had no LOW bucket at all -- and REFUSES rather than publishing the readable half when the scoreable share falls under the floor. STATED LIMITATION, registered now and not after the answer: a within-trace contrast spans a narrower density range than the between-trace contrast it is standing in for, 0.227 against 0.843, so a REFUTED here bounds the load mechanism at within-trace amplitudes and does not by itself prove the between-trace rise is instrumental.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE CLAUSE any scoreable group whose ratio points against the pooled verdict is NAMED with its numbers and its invocation counts, never absorbed. CONFOUND DECLARED BEFORE THE RUN, not after: the eager-issued kernels inside a captured trace are precisely those the capture could not absorb, so the two populations may differ in kind and in timeline position rather than only in issue mode. The instrument therefore reports, for each scoreable group and for each issue mode, the mean preceding-5ms device busy fraction, so a reader can see whether the two modes sit in comparable density; a group whose two modes differ by more than 0.20 in mean busy fraction is FLAGGED as density-confounded and its contribution to the pooled score is reported both included and excluded. THE RESIDUAL IS THE FINDING, and it says my attribution rule was wrong in a way the numbers make exact rather than probable. Of 48,929 device events in the trace, 4,793 join to an eager launcher and 156 join to a cudaGraphLaunch, leaving 43,980 with no runtime parent at all. The eager figure is exact to the event: 3,695 cudaLaunchKernel plus 1,026 cudaMemcpyAsync plus 72 cudaMemsetAsync is 4,793. The graph figure is exact too, and that is the tell -- 156 kernels for 156 cudaGraphLaunch calls is a ONE-TO-ONE join, which is not what a graph launch does: one replay issues thousands of nodes. So a correlation id identifies a CPU-side launch call, and a kernel executed as a graph NODE has no CPU-side launch call to be correlated with. The 43,980 unattributed are not a measurement gap, they are the graph nodes, and 43,980 of 48,929 is 0.899, consistent with the 0.9224 graph share of joined kernels recorded at this head. MY RULE TREATED ABSENCE OF A PARENT AS ABSENCE OF INFORMATION when absence of a parent IS the information, which is the same shape as reading an unexpressed class as a zero. The repair is not applied to this instrument: the predecessor verdict stands INCONCLUSIVE and the corrected attribution is frozen in a named successor.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE. Nothing about the instrument-versus-load question was decided; a wrong attribution rule refused before it could decide anything. SUCCESSOR, named and frozen rather than patched into the instrument that refused: graph-node-and-eager-issued-kernels-differ-in-duration-within-one-trace-20260916. Same cut, same group key, same thresholds, one changed rule -- a device kernel whose correlation resolves to an eager launch call is EAGER-ISSUED, and a device kernel with NO CPU-side runtime parent is a GRAPH NODE, because a replayed graph issues its nodes without a per-node launch call. Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
MORE THAN 50 PERCENT of the elementwise class's sized device time is spent in kernel invocations whose per-invocation working set EXCEEDS 72 MB. Such an invocation cannot be L2-resident by capacity alone, so if the bulk of the class sits there, the class genuinely touches DRAM, the aggregate excess is an artifact of a minority of small kernels, and the byte-reduction direction survives at something near its stated size.
Instrument
A bucketing pass over the elementwise population of an on-disk captured trace, reusing the join and the byte derivation of seat record: captured_elementwise_bandwidth.py: for each sized elementwise kernel, compute the per-invocation working-set bytes already derived there, bucket its device time by that figure against the 72 MB L2 capacity, and report the time share on each side plus the distribution. Analysis-only: no GPU, no lease, no new capture. NOTE OF RECORD -- the trace the 1,160.6 GB/s figure came from (cia-captured-trace-20260914T172624Z.json) is no longer on disk; this runs against cia-captured-trace-20260914T182441Z.json, a DIFFERENT capture. The class totals may therefore differ from the source receipt, and whether the aggregate rate reproduces at all on an independent capture is a second, unplanned reading this run produces.
Evidence
seat record: elementwise-l2-residency-20260915T0335Z.json
Result in full
The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF more than 50 percent of the elementwise class's sized device time is spent in kernel invocations whose per-invocation working set EXCEEDS 72 MB. It is 12.88 percent, across 9 kernels per step, at sized coverage 0.996. The criterion is not met, so the reading is SUPPORTED exactly as frozen. AND THE MECHANISM THE HYPOTHESIS PROPOSED IS REFUSED BY THE SAME DATA, which is reported here rather than left in the receipt. The explanation offered was that the above-DRAM aggregate is an L2 effect. If it were, the population that CANNOT be L2-resident by capacity would sit at or below the 1008 GB/s reference. It sits furthest above it: exceeds-L2 achieves 1390.9 GB/s against fits-L2 at 1146.8, and the >256MB bucket 1560.3. The likelier cause is an instrument property, not a cache one -- the byte model charges every sized input read once plus the largest written once, which over-counts aten::fill_ two-for-one and aten::copy_ three-for-two, and those two sites are 2,408.6 of the 3,522.1 us in the exceeding bucket. So the capacity question is answered and the residency question is not, and the aggregate excess over the published reference is at least partly an artifact of the byte model.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHAT THE REFUTED MECHANISM DOES NOT CLOSE. (a) L2 RESIDENCY IS STILL UNMEASURED. The elementwise row's not_closed line stands untouched: capacity is necessary and not sufficient, nothing here reads a cache counter, and 87 percent of class time being L2-resident-CAPABLE says nothing about whether a buffer survived between its producer and its consumer. What changed is that the above-DRAM aggregate is no longer usable as indirect evidence for residency, because the non-resident population exceeds the reference by more. (b) THE BYTE MODEL IS NOW THE LOAD-BEARING SUSPECT AND IS ITSELF UNMEASURED. Both this receipt and the one it extends derive bytes from recorded input dims, and the over-count is now known to be large enough to matter at the top of the distribution. A measured DRAM-traffic counter would settle it and this build has none. (c) THE BYTE-REDUCTION DIRECTION IS NEITHER CONFIRMED NOR REFUTED. It was the reason this cycle ran; the cycle failed to price it, because pricing it needs the residency answer the mechanism failure just removed the shortcut to. THE UNPLANNED FINDING, which is the cycle's real product: the class is BIMODAL. 1,844 of 3,336 sized kernels per step have working sets at or under 1 MB and take 2,269.4 us -- 8.3 percent of class time -- at 29.4 GB/s, 2.9 percent of the reference. Kernels between 8 MB and 72 MB are 1,004 per step and take 20,519.7 us, 75.1 percent of class time, at 1,202-1,261 GB/s. The bandwidth-bound ruling describes the second population and not the first. The small tail is the launch/occupancy population the row-1 framing was about, and it is 2,269.4 us: 1.4 percent of a 163,760 us governed step, far below the 1.5x arm bar, so it names which milliseconds belong to which story rather than nominating an arm. INSTRUMENT DEFECT FOUND AND CURED IN-CYCLE. The first run returned every kernel unsized -- that capture was taken without record_shapes -- and the script printed SUPPORTED, because an empty sized population makes the exceeding share 0.0 and the "more than 50 percent" criterion reads as unsatisfied. A verdict from an empty denominator is the persistent-lock-file defect inside a measurement. A coverage floor now refuses below 0.50 and names the cause; the refusal is receipted at elementwise-l2-residency-REFUSAL-20260915T0332Z.json, exit 2.

Methods, evidence and limitations
Criterion, frozen before the run
REFUTED IF the optimizer class REMOVABLE time -- measured optimizer device time per step MINUS the bandwidth floor implied by its own state footprint -- is BELOW 2,781.1 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE BAR AND NOT FROM THE DATA, and it is fixed here before any number is read: governed step 0.16376 s; 1.5x needs the step at 0.109173 s, a removal of 54,586.7 us; the two levers already priced supply all-device-idle 32,700.0 us and maximal elementwise fusion 19,105.6 us, capped composite 51,805.6; the shortfall is 54,586.7 - 51,805.6 = 2,781.1 us. That is exactly what a third lever must supply, so it is exactly the bar this class must clear to be the lever that decides the arm. THE FLOOR IS THE HONEST, MOST HOSTILE FORM OF THE COMPARISON. necessary_bytes = sum over the four AdamW tensors of trainable_elements x dtype_size, times the MINIMUM traversal count a correct fused AdamW must perform (read p, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write p, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq), and floor_us = necessary_bytes / (1008 GB/s) x 1e6 -- 1008 being the PUBLISHED specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling and never an impossibility premise. Using the published rate makes the floor as LOW as it can be and therefore the removable excess as LARGE as it can be, so the criterion is biased toward SUPPORTING the hypothesis; a refutation under it is a real refutation. SUPPORTED IF removable >= 2,781.1 us -- and the update must then say which sub-mechanism carries the excess (redundant traversals, an unfused path, state wider than the update needs, or a separate gradient-clearing pass), because "there is excess" names no treatment. INCONCLUSIVE IS RESERVED, and narrowly: only if the optimizer device kernels cannot be identified in the timeline at all, or the trainable-parameter footprint cannot be read from the inventory. A number that lands just under 2,781.1 is a REFUTATION, not an inconclusive result, and cycle 35 already proved the reverse case -- 19,105.6 against 21,886.7, ruled SUPPORTED at a 12.7 percent margin rather than softened. The same discipline binds in this direction.

Removable is 10,234.0 us per step, so the criterion is not met and the hypothesis is SUPPORTED. THE ARITHMETIC, every width measured rather than assumed. Measured optimizer device time is 16,817.8 us/step over 46.7 kernels across three symbols (fused AdamW multi_tensor_apply 15,847.4; _ForeachUnaryOp behind _foreach_zero_ 963.9; _ForeachBinaryOpScalar 6.5). The state archive was walked as a zip with a stub unpickler: 702 bf16 moment storages, 948,060,160 elements, 1,896,120,320 bytes, exactly 2.0000 B/elem, plus 351 single-element fp32 step counters. 702 moment tensors is 351 parameters x 2 moments, giving 474,030,080 participating elements -- which the manifest independently corroborates at 474,029,824 changed elements, 0.0001 percent apart, from a field this instrument does not use in its arithmetic. The parameter width was measured as a RATIO, not assumed: core 502,858,033 bytes plus expert objects 5,662,593,375 over 3,082,539,008 declared elements is 2.0001 B/elem, resolving to bf16 within the 0.02 tolerance the script refuses outside of. The minimum correct fused AdamW traversal -- read param, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write param and both moments -- is therefore 6,636,421,120 bytes, and at the PUBLISHED 1008 GB/s (a specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling for this card and never an impossibility premise) the floor is 6,583.8 us/step. 16,817.8 - 6,583.8 = 10,234.0 us, which is 3.68x the 2,781.1 us the bar needs from a third lever. No arm is named by this ruling.
Limitations, and what this does not close
WHICH SUB-MECHANISM CARRIES THE EXCESS -- the criterion required this, and the honest answer is partial, so it is given as one measured term, one ELIMINATED candidate, and one open remainder. A SUPPORTED verdict here closes nothing about routes either: it says the optimizer CONTAINS the 2,781.1 us shortfall with room to spare, not that any mechanism collects it. The three levers now priced (idle 32,700.0, elementwise 19,105.6, optimizer 10,234.0) act on different milliseconds only if they do not contend, and contention has NOT been checked -- the optimizer runs strictly after backward on one stream, which is precisely the serialization the idle lever claims, so these two may be pricing overlapping milliseconds and summing them would be the contending-ceilings error. That check is the successor and it outranks naming a treatment. NOT CLOSED, carried forward: no MEASURED device-memory traffic exists for these kernels, so the floor is an estimate of algorithmically necessary traffic, which the governed-run evidence contract requires to be reported separately from measured traffic; the gradient width is inferred from the parameter width rather than read from a receipt, though both hostile variants were run; the trace is a profiled run whose window span is instrumentation-dominated, so only per-step device figures are used and no wall-clock composition crosses that boundary; and the 128 aten::_fused_adamw_ calls against 1,195 param_groups is an unexamined shape that may itself be the redundant-traversal mechanism.

REFUTED IF the intersection of the elementwise and optimizer kernel sets, measured over the same six census windows by the two selectors VERBATIM as their own levers wrote them, is NONZERO -- specifically, if the pro-rated double-counted time exceeds 1.0 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS SET BEFORE THE NUMBER IS READ and it is deliberately near zero, because the claim under test is DISJOINTNESS and disjointness has no tolerance band: one shared kernel family means the stack was built by double counting, whatever its size. A nonzero intersection is a REFUTATION of the disjointness mechanism even if the corrected stack still clears the bar; the verdict is about the composition being sound, not about the bar being met. SUPPORTED IF the intersection is zero or below 1.0 us per step AND the re-derived timing check reproduces zero concurrency (sum of kernel durations equal to their interval union within 1.0 us per step). Both halves are required: the registry row that measured concurrency predates both levers, and a not_closed line is a claim about the past, so it is re-derived here rather than inherited. THE INSTRUMENT MUST REFUSE AN EMPTY SET RATHER THAN RETURN ZERO. An empty selector makes the intersection trivially zero, which would read as SUPPORT -- "the levers are disjoint" -- when it actually means the selector matched nothing. Opposite in meaning, identical in arithmetic. The script exits 2 on an empty lever set and --prove-red blanks the elementwise selector to prove that path fires before the green run. INCONCLUSIVE IS RESERVED, and narrowly: only if the trace carries no census_step windows, or if both selectors match nothing at all. A small nonzero intersection is a REFUTATION, not an inconclusive result. WHAT NO VERDICT HERE MAY CLAIM: neither outcome prices a treatment, names an arm, or establishes that the three removals are independent actions. Disjoint populations bound DOUBLE COUNTING only.

Limitations, and what this does not close
A DEFECT THIS CYCLE FOUND IN ITS OWN OUTPUT, disclosed because it is the more valuable half. The script printed "device idle inside windows: 373,323.4 us/step" from a window span of 503,890.3 us against 130,566.9 us of busy time. The governed-run evidence contract separation clause forbids exactly this composition, and the 32,700.0 us idle lever does NOT come from this number -- it comes from cycle 34 on a governed basis. So this census CANNOT corroborate the idle lever and does not try to; the idle line is printed for the busy/span arithmetic and is struck for every other purpose. (3) Each lever individually remains a CEILING under maximal effectiveness, not a measured effect: idle assumes every hole closes, elementwise assumes every intermediate stays in registers, and the optimizer figure is distance to a bandwidth floor under a published rate. Three perfect-effectiveness ceilings summing to 1.137x of the requirement is a thin result, and saying so is the point of this line. (4) One profiled trace, one geometry, no matched-run variation, so nothing here supports an improvement claim. (5) Both selectors are inherited verbatim from their own levers; if either mis-scopes its class, this census inherits that error exactly, and the 0.1 us agreement only validates the elementwise one.

RETIRES-EVERYTHING (the extreme bound, every optimizer launch gone): union hostile share 0.2338 -> 7,646.9 us, stack 54,392.7, DOES NOT CLEAR, short by 193.9 us. SO THE FINDING IS A DEPENDENCY, NOT A NUMBER: whether the three-lever stack reaches 1.5x under the hostile reading depends on the SHAPE of the optimizer treatment, a quantity nobody has specified. A bandwidth-floor optimizer that only widens each access retires no launches and the stack holds by 11.2 us; one that fuses the 963.9 us separate gradient-clearing pass retires launches and it can go short by up to 193.9 us. That dependency has to be resolved before any three-lever arm is authored, and it could not have been seen from either lever alone. Limitations, and what this does not close
A STRUCTURAL FACT IN THIS CYCLE'S OWN OUTPUT SHOWS THE HOSTILE ARM OF MY CRITERION IS LOOSE BY CONSTRUCTION, and it is confirmed rather than argued. The census reports 7,438.7 kernels per step and 7,437.7 gaps per step -- EXACTLY kernels minus one. So the in-window timeline is a single unbroken serialized chain with no coincident kernels and no zero-length gaps, which the instrument would have dropped. On such a chain, removing R interior kernels leaves K-R kernels and therefore K-R-1 gaps: EXACTLY R gaps disappear, never "every gap adjacent to a removed kernel". Removing one of a gap's two bounding kernels MERGES that gap with its neighbour instead of deleting it -- cycle 38 said this in its own docstring and then still froze a criterion on the adjacency count. The arithmetic confirms the identity: the conservative share 0.1576 equals 1,172.3 removed kernels over 7,437.7 gaps, 0.15762. The CONSERVATIVE measure is not a cautious lower bound at all -- it IS the structurally correct count, and the hostile measure is an artifact of counting adjacency instead of retirement. Under the correct measure contested idle is 5,152.6 us (RETIRES-NOTHING) or 5,357.7 us (RETIRES-EVERYTHING) and the stack clears by 2,300.4 or 2,095.2 us in both. THE VERDICT STAYS INCONCLUSIVE ANYWAY, and that is deliberate. The criterion was frozen before the numbers and binds on the hostile arm; re-reading it now against a derivation I made after seeing the result is exactly the move this loop exists to prevent, and it would be the move that converts an unwelcome verdict into a welcome one. The derivation instead becomes the SUCCESSOR, where it is frozen as the criterion BEFORE the run and the instrument is changed to measure retirement rather than adjacency. What that successor cannot do is claim novelty: the answer is already visible here, so it is scoped to confirming the identity on a second geometry and re-ruling the composition on the correct measure, not to rediscovering it. WHAT REMAINS OPEN. (1) The optimizer retirement fraction is still BOUNDED 0.0 to 1.0 and unmeasured, and resolving it needs the treatment SPECIFIED, not another trace -- this is now the binding prerequisite on any three-lever arm. (2) Applying a count share to a duration total still assumes contested gaps are of average duration; the correct-measure figure inherits that assumption exactly, and this trace cannot check it because its durations are instrumentation-dominated. (3) The BOTH-adjacent term used an independent-retirement reading, the largest lawful union; at 3.0 gaps per step it changes nothing either way. (4) All three levers remain MAXIMAL-EFFECTIVENESS ceilings rather than measured effects, so even a comfortably clearing corrected stack licenses an arm on ceilings. (5) One profiled trace, one geometry, no matched-run variation.
